_comment: The video tutorial catalogue. Edit this file to publish a tutorial: give an entry a `video` URL and set `ready` to true. An entry with ready:false renders greyed with a 'coming soon' note rather than being hidden, so the catalogue reads as complete instead of silently short — the same rule baja/lib/shelf.js uses. `video` may be a YouTube/Vimeo watch or embed URL, or a direct .mp4/.webm.
title: Video tutorials
subtitle: BajaBio RNATx Designer — short walkthroughs of the tools, grouped by what you are trying to do

books.title: A tour of the workspace
books.blurb: The canvas, the toolbar and the file browser: where tracks live and how a session is saved.

books.title: Loading a transcript
books.blurb: Find a gene by symbol or Ensembl id and put its transcript on the canvas.

books.title: Opening a VCF on the chromosomes
books.blurb: Upload a VCF, watch it place, and read the density strip beside each chromosome.

books.title: Selecting regions
books.blurb: Drag a range with Select sequence, or name a gene with Find gene, and collect several regions at once.

books.title: Highlighting by type
books.blurb: Show the protein-coding, intronic, UTR or pathogenic variants across the whole genome, with everything else greyed out.

books.title: Bookmarking views
books.blurb: Keep a place you want to come back to, and save it inside the karyotype file.

books.title: Allele selective ASOs
books.blurb: Pick a variant, choose a chemistry from the library, and tile allele-selective compounds across it.

books.title: Chemistry templates
books.blurb: Gapmers, uniform ASOs and siRNA duplexes: what the templates mean and how to add your own.

books.title: Reading a compound
books.blurb: The bead schematic, the backbone chemistry, and the target versus the synthesis strand.

books.title: Visualize clinical compounds
books.blurb: Load compounds like Spinraza and see them in the context of their genomics and chemical modifications.

books.title: Running off-targets on a group of ASOs
books.blurb: Take a set of designed ASOs, screen them against the transcriptome in one run, and read what comes back for each.

books.title: Variant annotations
books.blurb: Clinical significance, phenotypes, and where the red glow on a variant comes from.
